supplied.publicPrompt:
Play this logical combination game as a fresh player. Work toward the project shown by the public interface, choosing any legal route. You may stop when the project is complete or when you want to stop. There is no action-count target.

Use only the public CLI and its observations, rules, combinations and previews. Do not read model source, tests, analyst documents, witnesses, other players' records or solvers. Output filtering is allowed for reading the interface; do not write a program to choose moves.

Your session is fun-camp-persistent-ordinary-1. Initialize with:
node experiments/mars-progressive-camp-play.ts init fun-camp-persistent-ordinary-1 ordinary "$(cat results/mars-progressive-camp-prompts/fun-camp-persistent-ordinary-1.json)"
The metadata file is permitted setup data, containing this exact public assignment and your identifier.

Commands after initialization:
node experiments/mars-progressive-camp-play.ts view SESSION
node experiments/mars-progressive-camp-play.ts preview SESSION 'JSON ACTION'
node experiments/mars-progressive-camp-play.ts act SESSION 'JSON ACTION'
node experiments/mars-progressive-camp-play.ts checkpoint SESSION 'JSON REPORT'
node experiments/mars-progressive-camp-play.ts report SESSION 'JSON REPORT'
node experiments/mars-progressive-camp-play.ts finish SESSION

If the garden milestone is achieved while the overall project remains incomplete, record one brief annotation immediately before your next combination: your immediate aim, chosen action, expected result and confidence. Record the question verbatim as "What is your immediate aim, chosen action, expected result and confidence?" Do this only once; if both goals finish together, omit it.

After completion or your decision to stop, answer this open question using report: "What, if anything, was worth doing here, and what felt routine or unnecessary?" Record the question and your answer verbatim. If your answer does not already address earlier work, then answer separately: "Did anything you built earlier matter to what you did later? If so, what?" Label that second answer as prompted rather than spontaneous.

Then finish. Give an honest account, not praise you think the researcher wants. Your experience report is not a measurement of human enjoyment or duration. Do not extend play merely to supply more actions.

rules: This is a toy, not real Mars safety advice. There are no inventories, action limits, power budgets, hidden recipes or timers.

All concepts are inexhaustible. Combining named concepts establishes a reusable structured blueprint; both parents stay known. Installing it creates fresh component instances, not transferred identities from earlier installations.
Sunlight travels west to east. A clear shell encloses and transmits. Any reflective shell layer blocks transmission and redirects this sunlight north, using the fixed frame geometry.
All installed shells enclose the same designated camp and nest as layers. All lamps are inside all shells. At least one shell makes the toy enclosure; no air, temperature or biology is simulated.

Solar panels stay outside all camp shells. Their individual covers determine exposure. Each cable includes a sealed fitting. An uncovered/clear-covered panel powers only its connected lamp; power has no quantity or storage.
A powered interior lamp illuminates the tray. Its light also exits north/east/south/west if every shell layer transmits; any reflective layer blocks outward lamp light.
The northern observer receives northward rays and permanently remembers locating the camp. Current reception can later stop. This same receiver policy runs on both boards.

Known composite + world:camp installs a fresh actual copy without repeating its prerequisites. This places a known whole object; it does not show that the player synthesized its internal construction. Arbitrarily many copies remain legal.
Lamp + world:lead:ID connects a lamp to that installed lead. Clear sheet/reflective cover + world:shell:ID adds a boundary layer; + world:solar:ID covers that specific panel.
Existing layers remain: a clear sheet does not remove an opaque cover. An identical added layer on the same target has no new modeled effect and is not reoffered; new copies remain unlimited.
All legal actions and their exact results are public. Invalid actions do not alter construction or knowledge. Success does not prohibit further combinations.
The same physical camp, its installations, known blueprints and earned observer knowledge persist throughout this project. There is no next board or reset checkpoint.

argument.question: What, if anything, was worth doing here, and what felt routine or unnecessary?
argument.answer: The worthwhile decision was choosing a transmitting enclosure and then adding a powered lamp, so I could reach the observer without undoing the enclosed, lit tray. The clear shell I installed earlier stayed in place and mattered later: it preserved the enclosure while letting the lamp send light north. Building the solar lead and lamp felt routine because the recipes and effects were explicit; the interesting part was the interaction of shell transmission and ray direction, not discovering combinations. Extra shell copies, a combined lit-shell blueprint, and further play after completion were unnecessary for my route. This is an account of my choices as an AI agent, not a measurement of human enjoyment or duration.
